item.title: Siri AI Developer Preview Lets iOS, iPadOS, and macOS Apps Integrate with Siri
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/apple-siri-ai-integration/en/headerimage/ios-27-virtualization-1794583601204.jpeg"/><p>Apple released the Siri AI Developer Preview in the 27.3 beta releases of its operating systems, enabling developers and apps to integrate with the assistant and hand off actions to it. During the Preview, access to Siri AI is restricted to developer builds and internal TestFlight testers.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

item.title: Google Open Sources Ambient Quality Agent (AQuA) to Diagnose Production AI Agent Failures
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/google-ambient-agent-prod/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792894383462.jpg"/><p>Google has open-sourced AQuA, a reference implementation that analyzes production AI agent sessions, verifies recurring failure patterns, and investigates root causes against deployed source snapshots. In a 32-session replay, developers reduced seat selection bypasses from 15 sessions to two and dietary preference omissions from seven to zero after prompt changes.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

item.title: Netflix Turns Operational Data Into a Knowledge Graph for AI-Driven Observability
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/netflix-ai-driven-observability/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793693699423.jpg"/><p>Netflix is developing an ontology-driven knowledge graph to accelerate production investigations and provide AI agents with a shared understanding of its operational environment.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/bbc-software-architecture-influence/en/mediumimage/henry-wilson-medium-1792653480613.jpg"/><p>Henry Wilson shares actionable tools from the BBC Sounds re-architecture to help senior engineering leaders drive technical strategy. He discusses building buy-in, navigating active resistors, using RFCs and ADRs, and balancing tradeoffs - showing that effective software architecture is fundamentally about communication, relationship-building, and organizational influence.</p> <i>By Henry Wilson</i>

item.title: Podcast: Doing The Right Thing: Accountability In The Age Of AI Coding Summary
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/podcasts/accountability-age-ai-coding-summary/en/smallimage/engineering-culture-500-1794303925695.jpg"/><p>In this podcast, Shane Hastie, Lead Editor for Culture & Methods, spoke to Hugo Venturini about who is accountable when AI writes the code, how AI is reshaping code review and traditional engineering roles, and how leaders build a culture of transparency and psychological safety.</p> <i>By Hugo Venturini</i>

item.title: Dropbox Shares How Its In-House Cookie Auditor Tests Consent Behaviour Across 200+ Web Surfaces
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/dropbox-cookie-auditor/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794331089979.jpg"/><p>Dropbox engineers described a Playwright-based auditor that checks cookie consent behavior across more than 200 web surfaces. It runs three tests per page: US visitor, EU visitor, and Global Privacy Control signal. Cookie rules are kept outside the code. A companion tool finds live URLs. Weekly reports separate likely violations from false positives.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Technical Debt is Social; it is the Price of Learning by Doing
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/tech-debt-learning-doing/en/headerimage/header-1794404225270.jpg"/><p>Technical debt is not necessarily a sign of poor engineering. It can be the price of learning through software in use. As AI accelerates code production beyond our capacity to understand code and context, technical debt increasingly becomes a sociotechnical challenge.</p> <i>By Ben Linders</i>

item.title: Presentation: Opening the Black Box: Critical Explainability for AI Agent Tool Selection with Kiji Inspector
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/explainable-ai-llm-agent-decisions/en/mediumimage/HannesHapke-medium-1793278895069.jpeg"/><p>Hannes Hapke shares how Dataiku’s open-source Kiji Inspector applies Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) directly to decision tokens to expose why agents pick specific tools. Moving past superficial chain-of-thought narratives, he discusses causal ablation, layer activation extraction via patched vLLM engines, and production monitoring workflows for software architects and senior engineering leaders.</p> <i>By Hannes Hapke</i>

item.title: Azure Logic Apps Standard Gets a Local CLI in Preview
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/logic-apps-local-cli/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793791837422.jpg"/><p>Microsoft has released a public preview of the logicapp extension for the Azure CLI, adding local project creation, workflow authoring, a runtime lifecycle, connector management, run inspection, and test scaffolding for Logic Apps Standard, work that previously required the VS Code extension. The product team pitches the terminal surface as determinism for AI-assisted development.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Google Open-Sources TPU Sync for KV Cache and Weight Transfer on TPUs
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/google-tpu-sync/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794402814105.jpg"/><p>Google Cloud has open-sourced TPU Sync, a native C++ library that moves KV cache blocks and model weights between TPU HBM, host DRAM, shared storage, and the data center network.</p> <i>By Daniel Dominguez</i>

item.title: Author Q+A: finprim is a Case for One Financial Validation Library in TypeScript
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/finprim-validation-qanda/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793961374899.jpg"/><p>finprim is an MIT-licensed TypeScript library that offers IBAN, BIC, card, sort code, VAT, routing number and loan functions through one API with no runtime dependencies. Its author built it after duplicated validators drifted apart across web and mobile. It validates and formats data only, and does not process payments. He is cautious about adding SEPA and ACH file generation.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: LinkedIn Replaces Argo CD with a Custom GitOps Engine for Kubernetes Deployments
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/kubernetes-argocd-linkedin/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794414453878.jpg"/><p>In a recent post, LinkedIn revealed it has replaced Argo CD with its own GitOps engine. This new system deploys applications across over 250 Kubernetes clusters. It supports more than 4,000 services and manages over 100,000 deployments each week.</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

item.title: GitHub Makes Agentic Workflows Generally Available with Isolation and Budget Controls
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/github-agentic-workflows-ga/en/headerimage/header-1793990975266.jpeg"/><p>GitHub Agentic Workflows is generally available, running coding agents in GitHub Actions with read-only defaults and separately scoped write jobs. Those protections do not cover direct write permissions or custom jobs, so they depend on how each workflow is configured.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

item.title: JioHotstar Benchmarks Knowledge Bases for AI Coding Agents
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>JioHotstar evaluated 6 approaches to code retrieval for AI coding agents using SWE, CodeScale Bench, and an internal question-answering harness. Structural search performed well on concrete tasks, while semantic retrieval helped with ambiguous requirements. The findings highlight trade-offs in accuracy, token use, and tool design, underscoring the need to match retrieval tools to task types.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

item.title: How LinkedIn, Netflix & DoorDash Run Agents, Evals & Inference in Production: QCon AI New York 2026
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/qcon-ai-newyork-2026-program/en/headerimage/qcon-ai-new-york-2026-1794387431153.jpg"/><p>QCon AI New York has published its full program for December 15–16, 2026. Engineers from LinkedIn, Netflix, DoorDash, Figma, Pinterest, Honeycomb, Harvey, Google DeepMind and OpenAI describe AI systems they run in production. Talks cover agent permissions and guardrails, eval loops, inference cost, AI code review, and team adoption.</p> <i>By Artenisa Chatziou</i>

item.title: Presentation: Uncorking Queueing Bottlenecks with OpenTelemetry
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/opentelemetry-queue-observability/en/mediumimage/julian-oli-medium-1792652839179.jpg"/><p>Oli Lane and Julian Wreford share how Gearset replaced guesswork in distributed asynchronous queues with OpenTelemetry tracing. They explain why traditional metrics fall short, how to implement user-centric SLOs based on latency distributions, and share practical debugging tips to help senior developers, software architects, and engineering leaders improve system reliability and team culture.</p> <i>By Julian Wreford, Oli Lane</i>

item.title: Pinterest and Intel Take Open-Source Profiling to Internet Scale
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/pinterest-intel-profiling/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793692423906.jpg"/><p>Pinterest has partnered with Intel to extend gProfiler, an open-source continuous profiler that provides production performance visibility across an internet-scale fleet of infrastructure.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

item.title: Google Cloud Spend Caps Reach General Availability with API and Monthly Resets
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/google-cloud-spend-caps/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793609514337.jpg"/><p>Google Cloud has made spend caps on Cloud Billing Budgets generally available, pausing new usage of a service in a project once a monthly budget is hit, without deleting resources. GA adds an API, estimated live costs, and automatic monthly resets, but caps cover only the Gemini API, the Agent Platform, Cloud Run, and Cloud Run functions, and overages during enforcement delays are still billed.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Effect 4.0 Ships: Dependency-Free Rewrite with 5x Smaller Bundles and Long-Term Support
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/effect-4-0-release/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794245718049.jpg"/><p>Effect 4.0, a TypeScript framework for typed errors and structured concurrency, was released on 30 September 2026 with a rewritten fiber runtime. The team reports a bundle size drop from 35.6 kB to 7.1 kB and about 6.4x higher throughput, though these figures are not independently verified. It also adds long-term support through September 2029.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Entire's Git Forge Rethinks Git Collaboration for Coding Agents
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/entire-git-forge-coding-agents/en/headerimage/entire-git-forge-agents-1794134163813.jpeg"/><p>Entire is a Git forge designed specifically for collaboration between human developers and AI coding agents. Its premise is that traditional software development infrastructure, particularly the pull request (PR) model, is not well suited to an environment where AI agents generate, review, and iterate on code at high speed.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

item.title: Google Cloud Adds Self-Managed VMware Cloud Foundation on Bare Metal
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/google-cloud-self-managed-vmware/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793604325753.jpg"/><p>Google Cloud has made a self-managed VMware solution generally available, running VMware Cloud Foundation 9.x on dedicated Z3 bare metal with root access across ESXi, vCenter and NSX in 22 regions. It sits beside the Google-managed VMware Engine and matches customer-operated offerings from AWS and Oracle, shifting lifecycle, patching and Broadcom licensing back to the customer.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: GitLab 19.5 Makes Agentic Development a Governed Part of the DevOps Platform
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/gitlab-19-5-agentic-platform/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793095997884.jpg"/><p>GitLab 19.5, released on October 15, puts agentic software development and governance at the centre of the platform, making its GitLab MCP server generally available while expanding how external AI agents can interact with GitLab.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

item.title: TypeScript 7.1 Beta: Restores the Compiler API and Makes Vue and Svelte First-Class
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/typescript-7-1-beta/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793901816316.jpg"/><p>TypeScript 7.1 Beta, announced October 20, 2026, restores the compiler API removed in 7.0, now split into separate entry points. It adds content mappers, letting tools like Vue check non-standard files. One Vue project's type checks fell from 14.19 to 3.10 seconds. An editor issue remains open, and teams may need TypeScript 6 alongside 7.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: AWS Ships Continuum for Code Vulnerabilities
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/aws-continuum-ga/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792886107294.jpg"/><p>AWS has made Continuum for code vulnerabilities generally available in two regions. The service proves exploitability by running real exploits in a sandbox, then opens fixes as pull requests. Published pricing charges per finding processed as well as per line of code, and practitioners are asking what would justify letting it merge fixes on its own.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Vault Fork OpenBao Adds External Keys and Quantum-Ready TLS
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/vault-fork-openbao-27/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793734932785.jpg"/><p>OpenBao has released version 2.7, adding read scaling for PostgreSQL-backed deployments, support for external hardware security module (HSM) and key management service (KMS) keys, and post-quantum cryptographic algorithms. The release also introduces control groups for human review of sensitive operations and new headers intended to keep requests consistent across load-balanced OpenBao nodes.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

item.title: GitHub Actions Lockfiles Reach GA to Secure Workflow Dependencies
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/github-actions-lockfiles-ga/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793888107988.jpg"/><p>GitHub has made workflow dependency lockfiles for GitHub Actions generally available on October 28, 2026, two weeks after the feature entered public preview. Workflows can maintain clear tag and branch references.</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

item.title: Edera's Object Capability Bounded Authority Promises to Isolate Credentials from AI Agent Workloads
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/ai-credentials-isolation/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793853184587.jpg"/><p>Edera announced Object Capability Bounded Authority, a security model that separates an AI agent's or MCP server's required authority from the credentials behind it. Hypervisor-enforced capabilities limit agents to specific actions without storing secrets in the workload. Initial releases cover scoped command execution and workload identity; credential-brokered API access will follow.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>
